{"brief":"The user likes romantic comedies and has a strong interest in history, finding many World War II movies interesting. They enjoy learning why conflicts started, would watch documentaries, and describe themselves as a huge PBS fan. Recent viewing includes Sherlock Holmes movies and Dunkirk, the latter on TV; they gave no specific opinions on these films.

They have seen only parts of Wonder Woman on TV. They enjoyed its action and fun comedy, found Wonder Woman attractive, and appreciated her spunk and ability to take care of herself. They explicitly said they like assertive women.

The first Matrix interested them, with its mystery and the challenge of figuring out what was happening holding their attention. They thought the second and third films were nowhere near as good. They also felt it sometimes seemed “weird for weird’s sake,” despite holding their interest.

They are not a big fan of movie musicals. They dislike Aliens and refuse to go to horror movies, although they are unsure whether Aliens is classified as horror or sci-fi horror. Being frightened and jumping out of their seat are not entertainment to them; they do not want to pay to be scared.

They know little about The Shape of Water. They recall it being highly rated and think it won an Academy Award or two, but are uncertain. They said they did not get into it at the time or see many trailers and remarked on its unusual title. More exposure might have led them to watch it, but they explicitly said this was hard to judge with so little information. Their response should not be treated as a firm dislike."}
